deep.reconstruction:
Context. Over pages 135 to 137 Grothendieck proves the Hölder inequality for Schatten classes L^p(H) in the full range 0<p,q,r≤∞ (formula (6)): ||AB||_r ≤ ||A||_p ||B||_q when 1/p+1/q ≥ 1/r. This range includes the quasi-normed case p<1. The notation is as follows.
- For a positive trace-class T, M_T(ρ) = Σ_n α_n(T) ρ^n = det(1+ρT) is the Fredholm determinant, with α_n(T) = Tr Λ^n T, the elementary symmetric functions of the eigenvalues.
- S_x(T) = Σ λ_i(T)^x = Tr T^x. Formula (9) represents it, for 0<x<1, as the Mellin-type integral S_x(T) = (x/λ(x)) ∫_0^∞ log M_T(ρ) ρ^{-1-x} dρ, with λ(x) = π/sin πx. This follows from ∫_0^∞ log(1+ρμ) ρ^{-1-x} dρ = μ^x π/(x sin πx).
- S_r(X) = ||X||_r^r.

Step 1 (reduction). Since ||X||_r decreases in r, one may assume 1/p+1/q = 1/r. Take an integer m with p,q ≤ 2m, so that r/2m, p/2m, q/2m all lie in (0,1).

Step 2 (rewriting). Set L=(AB)*(AB), H=A*A, K=B*B. Then S_r(AB) = S_{r/2}(L) = S_{r/2m}(L^m), and by (9) this equals ((r/2m)/λ(r/2m)) ∫ log M_{L^m}(ρ) ρ^{-1-r/2m} dρ. This is (11).

Step 3 (Lemma 2, previous page). α_n(L^m) ≤ α_n(H^m) α_n(K^m). It is proved by passing to exterior powers, using Λ^n(AB) = Λ^nA Λ^nB, which reduces to n=1. The case n=1 is Tr L^m ≤ Tr H^m Tr K^m, obtained from the 2m-factor Hölder inequality for the trace together with ||X||_{2m} ≤ ||X||_m.

Step 4 (splitting). Hence M_{L^m}(ρ) ≤ Σ α_n(H^m)α_n(K^m) ρ^n. Write ρ^n = ρ^{n r/p} ρ^{n r/q}, which is possible since r/p + r/q = 1. Then bound Σ a_n b_n ≤ (Σ a_n)(Σ b_n) for nonnegative terms, which gives M_{L^m}(ρ) ≤ M_{H^m}(ρ^{r/p}) M_{K^m}(ρ^{r/q}).

Step 5 (next page). Take logarithms and change variables σ = ρ^{r/p}, then apply (9) again. This gives λ(r/2m) S_r(AB) ≤ λ(p/2m) S_p(A) + λ(q/2m) S_q(B), i.e. S_r(AB) ≤ [sin(πr/2m)/sin(πp/2m)] S_p(A) + [sin(πr/2m)/sin(πq/2m)] S_q(B). Letting m→∞ yields (14): ||AB||_r^r ≤ (r/p)||A||_p^p + (r/q)||B||_q^q.

This is a trace form of a Young inequality. Grothendieck calls it 'remarquable, mais n'est pas celle que nous cherchons'. It nevertheless gives Hölder at once by homogeneity: replace A by tA and B by B/t and minimise over t. Weighted AM-GM with weights r/p + r/q = 1 then gives ||A||_p^r ||B||_q^r.
errors: First line: 'A∈L^p A∈L^q' should read A∈L^p, B∈L^q.

Normalisation of λ: for (9) with factor x/λ(x), and for the final sine ratios, to be correct one needs λ(x)=π/sin(πx). If the page really reads λ(x)=π/(x sin πx), that is inconsistent with the later computations, which then give the wrong limit constant (r/p)^2. The reading is uncertain.

Gap or oversight: (14) is not a weaker result. By the scaling A→tA, B→B/t it is equivalent to the desired Hölder inequality (6), so the passage to m→∞ and the remark 'pas celle que nous cherchons' miss an immediate conclusion. The continuation on the next page may address this.
The requirement p,q ≤ 2m is needed so that p/2m, q/2m, r/2m lie in (0,1), where (9) converges. This is implicit but fine.

ideas.what: Integral (Mellin-type) representation of the Schatten quasi-norm Tr T^x, 0<x<1, through log of the Fredholm determinant det(1+ρT)
ideas.modern_name: Mellin transform / Stieltjes-type representation of x-th power via log det; operator-monotone integral representations
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (integral representations of t^x go back to Löwner, Heinz; determinant form not standard)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related material in 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956) and Produits tensoriels (Memoirs AMS 1955); unsure

ideas.what: Lemma: Tr Λ^n((AB)*(AB))^m ≤ Tr Λ^n(A*A)^m · Tr Λ^n(B*B)^m via functoriality of exterior powers. Taking m-th roots and m→∞ gives Π_{i≤n} s_i(AB) ≤ Π_{i≤n} s_i(A)s_i(B).
ideas.modern_name: Horn's multiplicative inequality for singular values (via antisymmetric tensor powers)

ideas.what: Trace Young inequality ||AB||_r^r ≤ (r/p)||A||_p^p + (r/q)||B||_q^q for all 0<p,q,r with 1/p+1/q=1/r
ideas.modern_name: Trace form of the matrix Young inequality (cf. Ando 1995 for the singular-value version, p,q>1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Equivalent to Schatten Hölder; matrix Young: T. Ando (1995)

ideas.what: Hölder inequality for Schatten classes including quasi-norm range 0<p<1
ideas.usually_credited_to: von Neumann/Schatten (p≥1); quasi-norm range via Horn/Weyl majorization, Gohberg–Krein, McCarthy (1967)

ideas.what: Reduction to the equality case 1/p+1/q=1/r by monotonicity of ||X||_r in r

missed.claim: Grothendieck's route to Schatten Hölder for p<1 replaces the usual Weyl/Horn log-majorization by generating functions. He uses Fredholm determinants det(1+ρT) and a Mellin integral of their logarithm, together with the coefficientwise inequality on Tr Λ^n. His Lemma 2 for all m implicitly contains Horn's inequality, so the page links Fredholm determinant theory with singular-value majorization. I do not know this proof in the literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a determinant-based, majorization-free proof of quasi-Banach Schatten Hölder inequalities. Such proofs could extend to settings with Fredholm determinants but no convenient singular-value calculus, such as Fuglede–Kadison determinants in von Neumann algebras. This is a minor methodological point.

missed.claim: Intermediate inequality with explicit finite-m constants: S_r(AB) ≤ [sin(πr/2m)/sin(πp/2m)] S_p(A) + [sin(πr/2m)/sin(πq/2m)] S_q(B). This is an unusual sine-weighted form, superseded in the limit.
missed.quote: S_r(AB) ≤ \frac{\sin π r/2m}{\sin π p/2m} S_p(A) + \frac{\sin π r/2m}{\sin π q/2m} S_q(B)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Curiosity only; it is weaker than the limit form (14).

deep.surprise_reason: The result, Schatten Hölder for all p>0, was essentially known by 1953 via Horn/Weyl. The method is original and elegant and seems unrecorded: a Mellin integral of the log Fredholm determinant, plus Λ^n-coefficient domination that secretly encodes Horn's inequality. It is a modest unpublished methodological detail, not a new theorem.
transcription_corrections: λ(x): likely π/sin(πx) for consistency with the rest; the reading 'π/(x sin πx)' is doubtful.
'Soit m un entier tel que p ≤ 2m, q ≤ 2m' is correct; the following struck/garbled line refers to 'lemme 2'.
The superscript '2m' near 'K = B*B' is a stray mark, not part of the definition.
